about: CHAIN pilots_secret (Design/content/chains/pilots_secret.md): the pilot of the Maas mouth teaches one man the bars from the Maas to the Vlie, and his price is not silver. Fourteen cards, 793 to about 815. Gerlef of Witla (cast.gerlef, witla.gerlef; invented, born about 745, dead in the winter of 812) is going blind. He will give the marks to one man for three things: a spring, a summer and an autumn of the boat; silence about his eyes; and an oath to put all of it into his grandson Gerbrand (witla.gerbrand, eight years old in 793) when the boy can carry it. Steps: he is asked about the water (s01); he misses the far mark (s02); he names his price (s03); the bar is sounded after the floods (s04); Thiadbod, who rents him by the year, offers silver for the marks (s05); the run north along the dunes (s06) and the verse of the marks at sea (s07); the Vlie has moved and the verse is wrong (s08); the schoolmaster of Saint Martin's wants the marks on a leaf after Bede's chapter on the tides (s09); the count wants a name beside the Maas on his list of river mouths (s10); the pilot is blind and asks whose the marks are (s11). Endings: the pole changes hands at Witla (end_boy, flag ch_pilots_secret_end_boy; or the marks kept from the boy, ch_pilots_secret_end_kept); the leaf after the tides at Traiectum (end_book, ch_pilots_secret_end_book; history changed: changed_bars_written, changed_bars_sounded_yearly); a master for the water at Dorestad (end_sold, ch_pilots_secret_end_sold; history changed on the count's road: changed_maas_kings_pilots). Progress is flags ch_pilots_secret_1 to _11; the wait between steps is the timed flag ch_pilots_secret_wait and the months of the sailing year. Needed for an ending: s01, s02, s03, then either s04, s06, s08 and s11, or s11 alone from 810; a house that began and did no more is still met by the grandson from 813 (end_boy). The forge names the people; the words call them Gerlef, Wilsuit and Gerbrand (the places file of Witla), Thiadbod (cast.thiadbod) and Count Folcbert (cast.folcbert). The words are in Data/writing/chain_pilots_secret.json; each option's note names the writing key of its outcome text. Sources are in the notes and the chain page. (?) marks what was not checked against a source. A draft for the user to overwrite. Written 6 Oct 2026.

cards.note: Step 1, the start: Witla, 793 to 806, in the sailing months (about Easter to Martinmas: places/witla.json 'seasons'), drawn on a call there once the house has called before. The pilot Gerlef (cast.gerlef), his daughter Wilsuit and her son Gerbrand are the places file's; all invented. 'A merchant who asks Gerlef about the water, and not about his price, can be taught what Thiadbod only rents' is the story witla.pilots_marks of the places file. The pilot: Old English ladmann, Old Norse leidsogumadr (lore/sea_lore.md 2). That Thiadbod pays him by the year is the spine's tie. Every answer starts the chain. Sets ch_pilots_secret_1; _asked.

cards.intention: The pilot of the Maas mouth sits in the door of his net shed and watches the bar. Skippers offer him silver to take them over it. Nobody asks him how he knows.

cards.note: Step 2: Witla, twenty days or more after step 1. The pilot's eyes: the spine gives his fear as going blind, and the places file has his daughter reading the far mark aloud 'as if by chance' and his line 'The far mark is soft this year. It is the haze.' The mark on the dune (a post held over the end of the ridge) is the site witla.mark; all invented. The fog riddle is riddles_793.json r-gest-05. Selling the word shuts the hard road of the first ending. Sets ch_pilots_secret_2 and one of _eyes_kept, _eyes_told, _eyes_sold.

cards.note: Step 3: Witla, from Michaelmas to Lady Day, when the wine ships have stopped. The price. That a craft went by mouth to one heir is the ordinary way of every craft without letters; that no sailing directions were written in the North before Ohthere's account (about 890, in the Old English Orosius) and none for these bars before the Low German Seebuch (about 1470) is lore/sea_lore.md 3 (?). The Vlie is the Fli of the Frisians' law (Lex Frisionum, about 802: 'between the Fli and the Sincfal'); Westflinge is the land west of it (first named 1064, dossiers/medemelacha.md) (?). The anchor riddle is riddles_793.json r-gest-06. The oath is sworn at the cross on the ridge (witla.cross), hand on the sounding pole: INVENTED. Sets ch_pilots_secret_3; _sworn; _bought_free.

cards.note: Step 4: Witla, March to May, after the winter floods. 'After the winter floods the pilot sounds the bar again, because the channel never comes back where it was' (places/witla.json 'seasons'). The craft: the pole in shoal water and the lead with tallow in its foot, which brings up the bottom (lore/sea_lore.md 3; Old English sundgyrd, sundline in the glossaries (?); Acts 27:28 for sounding); birds standing on a shoal, brown smooth water over the deep, a wrinkle with no wind over a bank (sea_lore 3, ordinary seamanship); the moon's place at high water ('At Witla you cross the bar when a full moon is in the south-east': the bearing is invented, the kind of rule is real and first written in the 14th and 15th centuries, sea_lore 5). The danger (a paying ship put on the bank) is warned of in a line. A failed check costs silver and a little heart and the story goes on. Sets ch_pilots_secret_4; _maas_true.

cards.note: Step 6: Witla, May to August, a month or more after the sounding. The run to the Vlie: outside along the dunes, or inside by the Kromme Rijn, the Vecht and the Almere to Medemelacha (dossiers/medemelacha.md 1: 'from Dorestad by the Kromme Rijn, the Vecht and the Almere to the Vlie'). Boniface crossed the Almere ('the water which in their tongue is called Aelmere') on his way to Dokkum in 754 (Willibald, Vita Bonifatii 8). That Gerlef had the Vlie marks from his wife's father is INVENTED. Outside, the timed flag ch_pilots_secret_aboard lets the sea card (s07) come. Sets ch_pilots_secret_6; _boy_aboard; _inside.

cards.intention: Between Whitsun and Lammas the weather is as steady as it gets. The pilot stands on the strand with his pole and a bag of bread. The Vlie, he says, is three days north with the dunes on your right hand, and he has not seen it in twelve years.

cards.note: Step 7 (optional): at sea, within twenty-five days of taking the pilot outside. The marks of the shore said as a verse: lists in verse are how the period kept what had to be remembered (the thulas of Widsith, the Old English Rune Poem). The verse itself is INVENTED. Its marks: the post at Witla (invented); the old stone in the surf off the mouth of the Rhine at Katwijk (the Roman fort later called the Brittenburg, seen at very low tides from 1520; its state in 800 is not known (?)); the old Rhine mouth was silting in these centuries and was shut in the 12th (?); Kinnem is Kennemerland; Adalbert's church is the chapel at Egmond over the grave of Saint Adalbert, died about 740 (?); Texel and Wieringen (Wiron) were not yet islands (dossiers/medemelacha.md 1). The rune stick: Frisian rune inscriptions on yew sticks of about this time are real (Westeremden, Britsum) (?); cutting sea marks on one is INVENTED and opens the second ending. The engine has no variable for which sea she is in: see 'needs' in the chain page. Sets ch_pilots_secret_7; _verse or _verse_slow; _stick; _shore_seen.

cards.note: Step 8: Medemelacha, May to October, after step 6. The Vlie: 'a narrow water between Friesland and Wieringen'; the Almere behind it fresh to weakly brackish; the king takes toll at Medemelacha from every trader sailing past, and a tenth of his income there (the regalis decima) is Saint Martin's of Utrecht, written in the church's goods register about 900 and most likely Pippin's grant of 753 (dossiers/medemelacha.md 1 and 5) (?). 'No bar, pilot or sea-mark is recorded' there (the same dossier): the moved channel, the fisherman and Saint Martin's boat going aground are INVENTED. What the card teaches is true of every such water: last year's marks may be wrong (sea_lore 7), and what lasts is the way of finding them. The danger (the old marks) is warned of in a line; failing costs silver and a little health and the story goes on. Sets ch_pilots_secret_8 and one of _vlie_true, _vlie_bought, _vlie_aground.

cards.note: Step 9 (optional): Traiectum, after the dune run or the Vlie. Saint Martin's and its school are real (Liudger was schooled there; Alcuin's poem greets it: dossiers/witla.md 7); the schoolmaster, an Englishman, and his boy scribe are INVENTED. What he reads is Bede, De temporum ratione 29 (written 725): the sea follows the moon; the flood comes later each day by four fifths of an hour, as the moon does; and the hour of the flood differs from shore to shore, as those who live on them know (our rendering; the chapter number and the fraction from memory (?)). Sounding in Acts 27:28. The scribe's complaint is the kind found in the margins of 9th-century books ('the parchment is hairy') (?). The moon's place at high water written for each bar is what later ages called the establishment of a port, first written in the North in the 14th and 15th centuries (sea_lore 5) (?). Dictating opens the second ending. Sets ch_pilots_secret_9; _written; _hours_written; _kept_mouth.

cards.note: Step 10 (optional): Dorestad, after the spring sounding. Count Folcbert (cast.folcbert, an invented man in a real office) and his clerk. In March 800 Charles left Aachen, went along the shore of the Gallic sea, set up a fleet on it and posted guards against the pirates (Annales regni Francorum 800); he went to Rome that autumn and was made emperor at Christmas. Einhard: stations and watches at all the harbours and river mouths where ships could come in (Vita Karoli 17). The coast from the Sincfal to the Vlie is the western part of the Frisians' law (Lex Frisionum, about 802). The Frisian's duty 'no further than the Weser to the east and the Fli to the west, out with the ebb and up with the flood' is from the Old Frisian laws, written down from the 13th century and older in matter (sea_lore 5) (?). The list of river mouths with a pilot named for each is INVENTED: royal pilots are a thing of much later centuries. Putting your name down opens the third ending. Sets ch_pilots_secret_10; _count_yes.

cards.note: Step 11, the choice: Witla, before 813. It comes ninety days or more after the Vlie, between Michaelmas and Lady Day; or, for a house that swore or gave its seasons and then stayed away, at any call from 810 (the old man is blind and tells from the doorway what he could not show). Gerlef dies in the winter of 812 (the places file). Each answer sets a road and a wait: the boy (always open), the leaf (needs the writing begun, the rune stick, or letters of your own), a master (needs the count's hundred or Thiadbod's hundred and fifty). Sets ch_pilots_secret_11 and one of _road_boy, _road_book, _road_sold.

cards.note: ENDING 1, the pole changes hands: Witla, at the spring sounding (March to June) sixty days or more after the choice; or, for a house that began the chain and never reached the choice, at any call from 813, when the grandson is the pilot and the old man is in the ground by the cross. Flag ch_pilots_secret_end_boy. This is what really happened, so far as anything here did: the craft went by mouth to one heir and nothing was written (no sailing directions in the North before Ohthere's account of about 890; none for these bars before the Seebuch of about 1470) (?). Gerbrand's sayings are the places file's ('Sound it twice...'; 'he said your father's house ... asked about the water first'). The plain road pays in a season's pilot fees and skippers' gifts. The hard road (sworn, the Vlie sounded by your own hand, the old man's eyes never sold) makes the two houses kin in the craft: a tie of fostering was the ordinary way two houses bound themselves; the lead is his own, with the hollow foot. The third answer keeps the marks from the boy and is an ending of its own, flag ch_pilots_secret_end_kept, with a lasting cost (ch_pilots_secret_witla_cold): the boy then learns the mouth from a man who can no longer see it, which is the fear the places file gives him. Grand rewards: unlock_pilot_maas and unlock_pilot_vlie on every road; unlock_kin_gerlefs_house and unlock_heirloom_gerlefs_lead on the hard road; unlock_upgrade_sounding_line on the third.

cards.note: ENDING 2, the leaf after the tides: Traiectum, sixty days or more after the choice. Flag ch_pilots_secret_end_book. HISTORY CHANGED: changed_bars_written. Nothing like it is known: the oldest sailing account of the North is Ohthere's and Wulfstan's, written at King Alfred's court about 890; the oldest directions for these very bars are in the Low German Seebuch of about 1470, full of depths and of what the lead brings up (sea_lore 3) (?). The Greeks' written coast-books (periploi) were known to Latin readers by name only (?). Bede's De temporum ratione 29 gives the rule of moon and tide and says each shore has its own hour, without the hours. On the plain road the leaf holds one year's marks and goes stale (ch_pilots_secret_leaf_stale). On the hard road (needs the Vlie sounded by your own hand) it holds the way of asking the water, and a rule that a brother sounds each bar at Easter and amends it: changed_bars_sounded_yearly. Both take the saint's boats, and in time other men's, away from the pilots of Witla (ch_pilots_secret_witla_cold). The third answer carries a copy to the boy, and the pilot's daughter keeps your goods on the strand. Grand rewards: unlock_pilot_maas, unlock_pilot_vlie and unlock_heirloom_leaf_of_the_bars on every road; unlock_title_st_martins_man on the hard road (the church's men were free of the king's dues at Dorestad by the privilege of 815, as chain house_debt has it; before 815 by the bishop's word (?)); unlock_factor_witla on the third.

cards.note: ENDING 3, a master for the water: Dorestad, thirty days or more after the choice. Flag ch_pilots_secret_end_sold. The count's road is HISTORY CHANGED: changed_maas_kings_pilots, sworn pilots of the king at a river mouth, with a writing of toll freedom at the king's post at Witla (that toll was taken there is Dijkstra's reading, not a record: dossiers/witla.md 1 (?)). Royal toll freedoms for named men and their ships are real (the abbeys' boats; Louis's letter for his merchants, 828); a pilot named by the crown is not heard of for centuries. It carries a duty that lasts (ch_pilots_secret_kings_duty). Thiadbod's road is nobody's history: the secret is bought, for twelve hundred pennies and the dry end of his dam head (the dams of Dorestad are parcels held by houses: dossiers/dorestad.md), and the Maas mouth is one house's water (ch_pilots_secret_thiadbods_water). Both leave Witla cold (ch_pilots_secret_witla_cold). The third answer costs only pride and both men's good opinion: it sets the road of the boy again, and the first ending opens at the next spring sounding. Grand rewards: unlock_pilot_maas and unlock_pilot_vlie; with the count unlock_charter_witla and unlock_title_counts_shipman; with Thiadbod unlock_plot_dorestad.
